key_insight: SJ-KAN analytically propagates spatial derivatives through a compact spectral network, achieving comparable or better Navier–Stokes solution accuracy with up to 47× fewer parameters and 8.2× faster training per epoch than the tested baselines.
engineering_relevance: This approach could reduce physics-informed training costs for incompressible flow simulation, including high-Reynolds-number lid-driven cavity cases without reference data.
method: Embed coordinates in Chebyshev bases and precompute their derivatives at collocation points.
Compress the bases into a few latent features using one linear layer, then predict physical variables with one nonlinear Chebyshev KAN layer.
Compute spatial derivatives analytically; use automatic differentiation only for weight-gradient backpropagation.
evidence_signal: Three variants were evaluated on the Taylor–Green vortex and lid-driven cavity benchmarks at Re = 100, 1,000, 5,000 and 10,000 against an AD-based PIKAN and a standard PINN; the Re = 10,000 cavity was solved without reference data using fewer than 9,000 trainable parameters.
watch_item: The abstract establishes results on two benchmark flows; performance on complex geometries and broader flow regimes remains unverified.
paper_title: SPARK: Spectral Preconditioned Analytic Residual Kolmogorov Arnold Networks for incompressible Navier Stokes equations
